title: The Frappe feature named Audit Trail is an amendment diff viewer
content:
The documentation describes it as *"A tool for viewing the changes made to a submittable doctype across multiple amended versions"*, tracking *"Fields Changed"*, *"Rows Updated"* and *"Rows Added / Rows Removed"*. The page makes no assertion about default enablement, immutability, hashing, chaining or protection from deletion.

This is a useful feature with a misleading name for anyone screening tools by keyword. The same trap appears in n8n, whose `/audit` endpoint is a vulnerability scanner. In both cases the word "audit" in a feature name says nothing about whether an append-only record exists.

The check that actually discriminates is not whether a tool has something called an audit trail, but whether its records survive the deletion of what they describe.
description: It shows changes to a submittable doctype across amended versions, with no claim of immutability, hashing or default-on behaviour anywhere in its documentation.
